newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. Council expected to authorize Albania force.
newsitem.headline: U.N. Council expected to authorize Albania force.

text.p: The U.N. Security Council is expected to authorize a European-dominated force for Albania to guard deliveries of food and other necessities and help the country recover from violence and near-anarchy.
Council president Zbigniew Wlosowicz of Poland said on Friday members were working on a resolution that he believed "would be ready for adoption soon, hopefully for tonight (Friday)."
He said the resolution would endorse a "multinational protection force that would facilitate prompt delivery of humanitarian assistance" to the Albanian people.

Several council members, after an informal session of the 15-member body, said China still had reservations about U.N. approval of a regional force and might abstain, and Japan and Sweden wanted more details and precision on the mandate.

Italian Ambassador Paolo Fulci, who is not a council member, circulated a draft resolution that called for U.N. authorization for a "temporary and limited multinational force to facilitate the safe and prompt delivery of humanitarian assistance and to help create a security environment" for that aid. The force would have a three-month mandate and is expected, at start, to have 2,500 personnel led by Italy.

Albania was swept by violence in January when a string of popular savings schemes collapsed, erasing millions of dollars. Rebels seized the south in March in an armed insurrection, blaming President Sali Berisha for the fiasco and demanding that he quit.
